Whether 100-80-100 holds here is decided by four conditions, and only
one of them sits outside our control.
Governing question: how many hours can this firm recover through redesign, and
what does removing the rest cost in client service?
The pilots’ main levers were shorter and fewer meetings with clearer
agendas, email-etiquette reform, protected focus periods and automated
reporting. Germany’s participants named meeting culture and reduced
distraction as their main efficiency levers.
Only 8% of Portuguese companies that made two or more organisational
changes reverted to five days, against 38% of those that made none or
one. Three-quarters made at least one change, and 87% reported active
Resignations fell from 2.0 to 0.8 per 100 employees in the UK pilot, and
Awin reports regrettable turnover down 33%. The most-cited UK
replacement cost, £30,614, is a 2014 figure and is not inflation-adjusted,
so any saving from it is illustrative arithmetic.

elements.text: The wellbeing result is established; the
Nothing in the public record establishes that revenue or retention
A controlled study of nearly 2,900 workers across 141
organisations in six countries found gains in burnout,
job satisfaction and mental and physical health that
were absent in its controls. Germany’s instrumented
pilot found the same falls in stress and burnout against
The UK 2022 report states that its resignation, new-hire
and absence trends cannot be called statistically
significant, given small sample numbers and
days, turnover and profit changed only slightly and not
Every revenue figure here is self-reported by the participating firm — an
assumption, not a finding. The standing pattern is documented in the primary
reports rather than asserted by critics: participation is self-selected by
management; control arms are absent, small or non-random; and follow-up
samples shrink, with 28 of 61 organisations at twelve months.
This evidence can justify a controlled trial. It cannot justify a commitment.
Sources: Autonomy UK pilot report (2023) · Fan et al., Nature Human Behaviour 9 (2025) · Germany pilot (2024)

The same trials are read as a transformative national success and as a

pages.name: Pilot 100-80-100 in two practice groups, after ten weeks of redesign

elements.text: Pilot 100-80-100 in two practice groups, after
Two whole practice groups, about 60 people (illustrative scope), on 100% pay
and a universal day off with a target 32-hour week. Ten weeks of redesign first,
six months of operation, one interim gate, and no change to contracts for the
The pilot is bounded in time and reversible at its interim gate.
8% of Portuguese companies reverted after two or more organisational changes,
against 38% after none or one. Two to three months of preparation is the norm.
A universal day off, not a flexible model.
Universal or staggered models converted to permanence in 95% of cases against
60% for flexible ones, on a sample the authors call too small for significance.
Half the Portuguese companies could not define productivity metrics at all, so the
metric set is agreed in redesign and published before the pilot starts.
Nearly half the permanent cases in the UK follow-up never changed contracts.
This pilot is stated as non-contractual in writing.
Kill criteria, agreed before the start and reviewed at the interim gate: client
satisfaction, on-time delivery, realisation, utilisation, voluntary attrition.
Scenario data — thresholds are the firm’s to set and are illustrative here.
a firm-wide permanent commitment, which has no evidence at this scale or
